# Blackline 0.15.45

The rest of the list, and three things that were wrong in what shipped before it.

## Three fixes, two of them in builds you already have

**Roles could not be created or edited.** `bl-proto` keeps its own list of the grant names a signed
space record may carry, and it is checked before a record is accepted. The seven permissions added in
0.15.42 were never added to that list, so every role record naming one was refused as malformed —
which meant **no role could be made or changed in 0.15.42, 0.15.43 or 0.15.44**. Found by the
three-core space test, fixed, and both the wire list and the core list now carry all thirty. The list
says in its own comment that a new permission must be added to both.

**Invites did not last as long as they said.** 0.15.42 let an invite be made for up to thirty days,
but the transport's one-time code underneath always expired after fifteen minutes — so a seven-day
invite looked alive and was a dead letter after a quarter of an hour. The code now carries its own
lifetime and matches the invite exactly.

**Onboarding stopped waiting on the username claim.** Claiming a name is proof of work — several
seconds — and then a fetch from the mirrors. Doing it before the address screen meant a new account
sat on a spinner for ten to twenty seconds, longer if the registry was slow. The account exists the
moment the keys do, so the address is shown the moment the keys do; the claim runs behind it and says
where it got to.

## The members page

A table, with what the space actually knows: when somebody joined, what they hold, and whether they
are reachable. Tick several and time out, kick or ban them together — each is still its own signed
record, so it says how many it is about to do before it does any of them. Sort by name, by when they
joined, or by rank. At a narrow width the columns fall away rather than squeeze.

Two of the columns a server list usually has are missing on purpose. There is no date somebody
"joined Blackline" — there is nothing to join but spaces and people. And nothing here watches
anybody, so there is no behaviour score to show.

## Join requests

A space can **ask before letting people in**. An invite then brings somebody to the door rather than
through it, and anybody holding *approve joins* lets them in or turns them away. Until then they hold
no keys and see nothing.

Whoever is waiting is kept on the approver's device rather than in memory — a request that vanished
when the app restarted would leave somebody waiting at a door nobody could see them at. Turning
somebody away tells them, and their pending tile goes, rather than waiting for keys that are never
coming.

Nobody can find a space without an invite either way. There is nothing to search.

## Role pills

One pill, everywhere: the name, then its colour as a circle on the right. One function draws it, so a
role on a profile card and a role in the members table cannot drift apart.

## Not done, and why

**Short invites.** I traced it rather than guessed. The receiving side already keys off the nonce
alone, so the long blob exists only so the *joiner* can reach the inviter. There are three ways to
reach somebody: the blob, which carries addresses and keys; a bare address, which only registers
interest and waits to be knocked on, so it can never present a code; or a registry username. Only the
last could give a short code, and it would mean space invites worked only for people who have claimed
a username — plus a dial-with-nonce path that does not exist. That is a trade worth deciding on, not
one to make quietly.

## The test suite

Seven assertions across five tests described behaviour that had deliberately changed and had not been
updated with it — read receipts being a word rather than a tick, Delete being offered on messages it
cannot delete, twenty-three permissions, remote control being "not in this version", a name that a
47-character invite cannot carry, a menu missing an item, and a block taking away a conversation the
store keeps on purpose. Each was updated to describe what the app now does, with the reason, rather
than loosened.
